phases.name: 1. Scope and entry path
phases.description: Turn the saved traffic and latency brief into a redirect path that can be scaled independently of link creation.

phases.name: 2. Unique, permanent mappings
phases.description: Reserve generated and custom codes without races, store mappings permanently, and make the read cache disposable.

phases.name: 3. Asynchronous click analytics
phases.description: Move click collection and aggregation off the redirect response while preserving useful owner analytics.

phases.name: 4. Availability and operating limits
phases.description: Add SLO signals, multi-zone recovery, and a concrete response to a hot read tier.

phases.name: 5. Owner analytics access and review
phases.description: Expose eventual analytics through an owner-authorized service path without adding work to redirects.

steps.title: Read the brief before choosing a database
steps.content: The saved exercise requires 100M **new URLs per day**, a 100:1 read/write ratio, redirects under 100ms, 99.9% availability, custom aliases, analytics, and links that do not expire. That is about 1.2k creates/s and 116k redirects/s on average before peak headroom. We will treat <100ms as a regional p95 design target, not a measured global guarantee. The write path must establish one durable code-to-destination mapping; the read path must stay short even if analytics is slow.

steps.title: Add browsers and API clients
steps.content: Owners create links through an authenticated API. Visitors follow a short URL without logging in. Separating these two request classes lets us rate-limit creation more strictly without slowing public redirects.

component.label: Browsers & API Clients
component.description: Authenticated link creators and anonymous redirect visitors

properties.purpose: Create links and follow short URLs over HTTPS; redirect visitors do not require an account.

component.highlightReason: The two user paths have different authentication and latency needs.

steps.title: Add an edge tier
steps.content: The edge terminates TLS, rejects abusive traffic, and routes to healthy regions. It may cache safe redirect responses briefly, but it must not be the authoritative mapping store. A stale edge response is bounded by the cache policy, while a permanent link is retained in the primary store.

component.label: Edge Redirect Tier
component.description: TLS, abuse filtering, and short-lived redirect caching

properties.purpose: Terminate TLS, reject abusive traffic, route to healthy regions, and cache only safe redirects briefly; the permanent mapping remains in the primary store.

component.highlightReason: The 100:1 read-heavy workload needs a fast edge and independent origin.

steps.title: Route client traffic to the edge
steps.content: Both create and redirect requests arrive via HTTPS. The edge can distinguish authenticated API traffic from anonymous short-code lookups.

connection.label: HTTPS create / redirect
connection.description: TLS-protected public entry; anonymous visitors use GET /{code}.

steps.title: Add the API gateway
steps.content: The gateway validates create requests, enforces owner quotas and safe destination URL schemes, and dispatches redirects without authentication. Keep expensive click counting out of this synchronous hop.

component.label: URL API Gateway
component.description: Create validation, quotas, and redirect routing

properties.purpose: Validate POST /links and allow only http/https destinations; authenticate and rate-limit creators, while GET /{code} remains anonymous. Keep click counting off this synchronous path.

component.highlightReason: Creation security and public redirect latency require different policies.

steps.title: Connect edge to gateway
steps.content: A cache miss or create request reaches the gateway; an edge hit can answer without this hop.

connection.label: Origin request on miss
connection.description: Pass create requests and redirect cache misses to the regional API gateway.

steps.title: Add a regional load balancer
steps.content: Spread stateless application requests across instances and stop routing to unhealthy nodes. Multi-zone placement is required to make the 99.9% availability target credible.

component.label: Regional Load Balancer
component.description: Health-aware distribution across stateless URL services

properties.purpose: Route to healthy URL service instances across availability zones.

component.highlightReason: One instance or zone must not become the redirect availability bottleneck.

steps.title: Connect gateway to service pool
steps.content: The gateway passes a validated request to the load-balanced service pool.

connection.label: Validated URL request
connection.description: Route create and redirect requests to healthy service instances.

steps.title: Add the URL service
steps.content: One stateless service owns create and redirect semantics. `POST /links` returns the reserved short URL only after the mapping is durable. `GET /{code}` resolves cache-first and returns a redirect; unknown codes return 404. Do not acknowledge a new alias before its uniqueness write succeeds.

component.label: URL Service
component.description: Durable link creation and cache-first redirect resolution

properties.purpose: Statelessly create permanent code mappings through POST /links only after a durable uniqueness write; resolve GET /{code} cache-first with 302 for known codes and 404 for unknown codes; emit click events asynchronously.

component.highlightReason: Separates correctness of mapping creation from the much hotter redirect read path.

steps.title: Connect load balancer to URL service
steps.content: Any healthy service instance can handle any code; no sticky routing is required.

connection.label: Create or resolve
connection.description: Stateless request dispatch to an available URL service instance.

steps.title: Separate code assignment from resolution
steps.content: Generated codes can be Base62-encoded IDs; custom aliases use the same normalized code namespace. A simple read-then-write check is racy. Both paths must reserve through one atomic uniqueness operation against the authoritative store. Base62 keeps identifiers compact; capacity and collision behavior must be monitored as the namespace grows.

steps.title: Add the code and alias allocator
steps.content: The allocator issues compact generated IDs and normalizes custom aliases. It never promises availability merely from a cache lookup; the store decides uniqueness. Generated-ID blocks can be leased per instance, but their committed mappings remain globally unique.

component.label: Code & Alias Allocator
component.description: Base62 IDs and normalized custom-alias reservation

properties.purpose: Generate distributed unique IDs, encode generated values as Base62, and normalize custom aliases; the authoritative store conditionally reserves both in one shared namespace.

component.highlightReason: Custom aliases and generated codes must share a collision-safe namespace.

steps.title: Ask the allocator to reserve a code
steps.content: Creation calls the allocator; redirect lookups do not. Keeping allocation off the hot read path protects latency.

connection.label: Reserve generated/custom code
connection.description: Choose a candidate code for the create path only.

steps.title: Choose an atomic alias policy
steps.content: Apply the decision to the allocator: normalize case according to a documented policy, reject reserved words, then use a conditional insert. On a generated-code conflict retry with a fresh ID; on a custom-alias conflict return 409 rather than silently changing the user's choice.

decision.question: How do concurrent creators avoid claiming the same short code?
decision.chosen: One conditional write for both generated and custom codes
decision.chosenReason: The authoritative store serializes the uniqueness decision without a read-before-write race.

alternatives.tradeoff: Two concurrent requests can both observe an unused alias and race.
Collision probability grows and a wrong redirect would be unacceptable.

properties.purpose: Generate distributed unique IDs, encode generated values as Base62, and normalize custom aliases; the authoritative store conditionally reserves both in one shared namespace. Generate distributed Snowflake IDs and encode them as compact Base62 codes; normalize custom aliases and reject reserved words. The authoritative store conditionally reserves both in one shared namespace, retries generated-code collisions, and returns HTTP 409 for a requested alias conflict.

steps.title: Add the authoritative link store
steps.content: Partition mappings by short code for direct lookup. Store destination, owner, creation time, status, and an idempotency key for create retries. Replicate durably across zones; do not put an expiry TTL on the authoritative mapping because the saved brief explicitly says URLs do not expire.

component.label: Permanent Link Store
component.description: Unique code-to-destination mapping and owner metadata

properties.purpose: Authoritative mappings keyed by normalized short code for direct lookup. Store destination, owner, creation time, status, and idempotency data; conditional create prevents duplicates. Mappings are permanent and replicated across zones.

component.highlightReason: The mapping must survive cache eviction, process failure, and long-lived links.

steps.title: Reserve the code in the link store
steps.content: The allocator performs the conditional create against the code key. A successful commit is the point at which the short URL becomes valid.

connection.label: Conditional code insert
connection.description: Atomically reserve one code and destination; reject an existing custom alias.

steps.title: Resolve cache misses from the link store
steps.content: On a cache miss, the URL service reads by short code and fills the cache. Store errors should fail closed rather than redirecting to an unverified destination.

connection.label: Mapping lookup on miss
connection.description: Read the authoritative destination when the redirect cache has no valid entry.

steps.title: Add the redirect cache
steps.content: Most lookups should avoid the primary store. Cache successful resolutions by code with a bounded TTL; negative-cache missing codes briefly to reduce repeated abuse. Cache eviction is not URL expiry, and a cache outage falls back to the durable store.

component.label: Redirect Cache
component.description: Read-heavy short-code lookups with bounded TTL

properties.purpose: Use cache-aside lookup for code-to-destination mappings with a 300-second positive TTL and 15-second negative TTL. Cache eviction never expires a link; cache failure bypasses to the permanent store.

component.highlightReason: The 100:1 read/write ratio and <100ms target make cache hits central to capacity.

steps.title: Read the cache before storage
steps.content: A redirect performs one cache lookup, then a direct store lookup only on miss; the service responds with a 302 without waiting for analytics.

connection.label: Cache-first code lookup
connection.description: Fast code lookup with store fallback on miss or cache failure.

steps.title: Keep links permanent
steps.content: The current saved problem says URLs should not expire. Record that decision on the authoritative store: no TTL or default deletion policy. A future product revision could add optional expiry, but it is **not** silently introduced into this exercise.

decision.question: Should short links expire automatically?
decision.chosen: No automatic expiry in this brief
decision.chosenReason: The active catalog constraint explicitly says URLs should not expire; cache TTL does not delete a mapping.

alternatives.tradeoff: Useful in another product scope, but contradicts the current saved constraint unless that brief is revised.

properties.purpose: Authoritative mappings keyed by normalized short code for direct lookup. Store destination, owner, creation time, status, and idempotency data; conditional create prevents duplicates. Mappings are permanent and replicated across zones. Store permanent mappings keyed by normalized short code, including destination, owner, creation time, status, and idempotency data; conditional create enforces uniqueness. Mapping records never expire or receive a TTL, and cache eviction never deletes the authoritative record.

steps.title: Control a hot redirect key
steps.content: Apply a bounded cache policy and single-flight fill for popular or missing codes. An empty cache should warm from the store without causing a thundering herd, and a cache node failure should not make every URL appear expired.

properties.purpose: Use cache-aside lookup for code-to-destination mappings with a 300-second positive TTL and 15-second negative TTL. Cache eviction never expires a link; cache failure bypasses to the permanent store. Use cache-aside reads with single-flight miss filling and replication for hot keys. Keep positive entries for 300 seconds and missing-code entries for 15 seconds; on cache failure, read from the durable link store.

steps.title: Protect the redirect from analytics work
steps.content: Click count and location are useful but can be eventually consistent. The redirect should return once the destination is known; enrichment, geolocation, and aggregation are background work. If click ingestion is unavailable, favor a successful redirect and surface an analytics-lag alert instead of making navigation fail.

steps.title: Add the click event queue
steps.content: Record privacy-scoped click events with code, coarse location, timestamp, and deduplication ID. Buffer spikes so a popular link cannot force synchronous writes into the analytics store.

component.label: Click Event Queue

properties.purpose: Durably buffer privacy-scoped click events partitioned by short code for at-least-once asynchronous processing. Retain events for 72 hours; redirect success does not wait for analytics.

component.highlightReason: Analytics is eventually consistent and must not extend redirect latency.

steps.title: Emit clicks after resolving the destination
steps.content: The service emits a best-effort event after resolution. Duplicate delivery is possible, so consumers deduplicate by event ID. Queue health is observed separately from redirect health.

connection.label: Async click event
connection.description: Queue a click event without blocking the redirect response on aggregation.

steps.title: Add analytics workers
steps.content: Workers enrich coarse location, filter bots according to policy, deduplicate retries, and aggregate counts per link/time bucket. This pool scales with queue lag independently of redirects.

component.label: Analytics Workers

properties.purpose: Consume click events, deduplicate by event ID, enrich only coarse location, and aggregate counts by link/time bucket. Scale this worker pool on queue lag, independently of redirects.

component.highlightReason: Off-path processing provides analytics without slowing public redirects.

steps.title: Consume click events
steps.content: At-least-once delivery requires idempotent updates; a worker restarts from its cursor without double-counting.

connection.label: Consume and dedupe
connection.description: Workers process queued click events and acknowledge after durable aggregate writes.

steps.title: Add the analytics store
steps.content: Serve link-owner dashboards from pre-aggregated counts and location buckets. It is not the mapping authority; an analytics outage must not make short URLs unresolvable.

component.label: Analytics Store
component.description: Eventually consistent click and location aggregates

properties.purpose: Persist eventually consistent per-link, per-time-window click counts and coarse location aggregates, partitioned by short code and time bucket. This store is rebuildable and never authoritative for redirects.

component.highlightReason: Separate reporting storage from the latency-critical link mapping store.

steps.title: Persist aggregate views
steps.content: Workers update idempotent aggregates; dashboards can show an 'updated as of' timestamp when queue lag grows.

connection.label: Click aggregates
connection.description: Write rebuildable count and location summaries for owner analytics.

steps.title: Add service health monitoring
steps.content: Track redirect p95/p99, cache hit ratio, store latency, alias conflicts, error rates, queue lag, and availability by zone. Measure the <100ms and 99.9% targets from real requests, not from a diagram label.

component.label: Redirect SLO Monitoring
component.description: Latency, availability, cache, collision, and analytics-lag signals

properties.purpose: Alert on redirect latency against the 100 ms target, 5xx errors, cache misses, store errors, alias conflicts, queue lag, and availability against the 99.9% target.

component.highlightReason: Reliability and latency claims need observable operating signals.

steps.title: Export service metrics
steps.content: Monitor the redirect and create paths separately so a reporting backlog is not mistaken for a broken redirect service.

connection.label: Redirect and create SLOs
connection.description: Emit request latency, availability, cache/store errors, and alias conflict metrics.

steps.title: Choose multi-zone durability
steps.content: A permanent link must survive an instance or zone failure. Replicate the authoritative mapping across zones, maintain tested backups, and route around failed service instances. Cross-region failover is a later availability/consistency tradeoff, not a free assumption.

decision.question: What does 99.9% availability require beyond a load balancer?
decision.chosen: Multi-zone durable mapping store with tested recovery
decision.chosenReason: Redirects are only available when the authoritative mapping remains readable after a zone failure.

alternatives.tradeoff: A zone failure makes both new links and cache misses fail.
Custom alias uniqueness becomes harder and needs an explicit conflict-resolution policy.

Store permanent mappings keyed by normalized short code, including destination, owner, creation time, status, and idempotency data; conditional create enforces uniqueness. Mapping records never expire or receive a TTL, and cache eviction never deletes the authoritative record. Keep permanent mappings readable across an availability-zone failure, with tested backups and point-in-time recovery. steps.title: Scale before a hot-cache collapse
steps.content: If cache hit rate drops or p95 redirect time approaches the 100ms target, add cache capacity and protect the store with bounded concurrency and request coalescing. At the stated 100:1 ratio, a total cache miss can overwhelm origin even when creates are healthy.

scaleTrigger.action: Add regional cache capacity, coalesce misses, and cap direct-store concurrency
scaleTrigger.impact: Protects the authoritative store while keeping the redirect path under its latency budget.

properties.purpose: Statelessly create permanent code mappings through POST /links only after a durable uniqueness write; resolve GET /{code} cache-first with 302 for known codes and 404 for unknown codes; emit click events asynchronously. Statelessly create permanent mappings through POST /links only after durable uniqueness succeeds; resolve GET /{code} cache-first with 302 for known codes and 404 for unknown codes; emit click events asynchronously. Coalesce cache misses and bound direct-store concurrency for the stated 100:1 redirect-to-create ratio.

steps.title: Read analytics through the URL service
steps.content: Only an authenticated owner asks for reports. The service reads the separate, eventually consistent aggregate store and returns a bounded time-window result; this query is never part of public redirect resolution.

connection.label: Owner analytics query
connection.description: Owner-authorized GET /links/{code}/analytics reads eventual aggregates via the service, outside the redirect path.

steps.title: Define the owner analytics endpoint
steps.content: Authorize each report against link ownership, bound the time range and result size, and disclose that recent counts may lag while queue events are processed.

Coalesce misses and bound origin concurrency for the 100:1 read ratio. Also expose GET /links/{code}/analytics only to the link owner, with a bounded time range/result size and disclosed aggregate freshness; keep reporting off the redirect path.

steps.title: Review the create, redirect, and reporting paths
steps.content: **Create:** authenticated client → edge/gateway → URL service → allocator → conditional mapping write; return the code after commit. **Redirect:** visitor → edge cache or URL service → cache/store → 302; enqueue a click independently. **Reporting:** an owner calls the authenticated analytics endpoint and reads a separate eventual aggregate view. Cache/store failures must not produce false redirects, and analytics lag must not stop navigation. The active brief has no link expiry; if the product later wants optional expiration, revise the problem and then version this guide.
